rows.fidelity_note: The interior height weight is (r−r₁)(1−η²), where η is the height reference coordinate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInnerWeight

rows.fidelity_note: The radial interior form uses integration by parts and the inverse test Gram matrix, with radial degrees below Q−1 and height degrees through Q. This family is empty when Q≤1.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialInnerForm

rows.fidelity_note: The height interior form uses the differentiated weighted tests and their Gram matrix, with both test degrees below Q.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInnerForm

rows.fidelity_note: The outer radial test is w(r)rʲzˡ, where w is the axis-dependent polynomial measure.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterTest

rows.fidelity_note: The outer radial row combines both face moments with the interior derivative of rξ times the weighted test. The endpoint values ξ=−1 and ξ=1 account for the two positive face terms.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterRow

rows.fidelity_note: The outer radial derivative form pairs these boundary rows through the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical measure r dr dz.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterForm

rows.fidelity_note: The outer height row combines the two height-face moments with the negative height derivative of rηrʲzˡ in the interior.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOuterRow

rows.fidelity_note: The outer height form uses the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical weight r and test degrees through q radially and through Q vertically.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOuterForm

rows.fidelity_note: The axis-compatible angular test is r^(j+1)zˡ, obtained by multiplying the meridian monomial by r.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularTest

ties.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularAxisForm
ties.plain: Angular energy on an axis cell

rows.fidelity_note: The angular form on axis cells uses the r-weighted Gram matrix of axis-compatible tests. Its bounds come from their pairings with the known coefficients.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularAxisForm
rows.plain: Angular energy on an axis cell

rows.fidelity_note: The off-axis angular weight is (r₂−r)/(rr₂). It is nonnegative on a valid off-axis interval and vanishes at r₂.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOffWeight

rows.fidelity_note: The off-axis angular form adds the diagonal contribution 1/r₂ to a remainder obtained from tests weighted by (r₂−r)/(rr₂).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOffForm

rows.fidelity_note: The component energy adds radial, height, and angular contributions. Axis cells omit the off-axis interior terms and use the axis-compatible angular tests.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.componentForm

rows.fidelity_note: The penalty selects the upper polynomial-degree strips in the radial and height columns of the gradient. When Q=0, the lower threshold Q−1 is taken to be zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.topForm

rows.fidelity_note: For each mode, the form adds weighted gradient and curl derivative energies and subtracts the designated highest-degree penalty. The result is then summed over the resolved modes.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.energyForm

rows.fidelity_note: A low polynomial coordinate belongs either to a gradient component with degrees through Q or to a velocity component with degrees below Q.

ties.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotValue

rows.fidelity_note: The polynomial space consists of complex functions with degree at most d in r and at most d′ in z. Its description is by the existence of a finite coefficient expansion.

rows.fidelity_note: The weighted pairing is ∫_Q m F conjugate(P) dr dz, with conjugation on the test function.

ties.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.lineWeightFn

rows.fidelity_note: The tail square is the weighted integral of |F−Π_QF|², where the projection includes degree Q in both meridian variables.

rows.fidelity_note: The local value is Re(U*AU) on the 12 gradient-and-velocity coordinates, with conjugation on the first factor.

rows.fidelity_note: A row has one of seven justifications: shared boundary data, subdivision, a flux identity, a relation, a normal-derivative identity, direct cell data or absence from all relevant forms.

rows.fidelity_note: This marks a row as unused. The separate unused-row conditions require its coefficients and all matrix and credit contributions to vanish.

rows.fidelity_note: Each row has finite support, complex coefficients, a specified justification and a rank ordering its dependencies. Separate selections identify forcing, pin and port unknowns.

rows.fidelity_note: The data specify finite support of global perturbation-determined coordinates for each cell row.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry

rows.fidelity_note: Only coefficients inside the declared finite support are retained; the row is zero outside that support.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.rowVec

rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.rowValue
rows.plain: Evaluate a row on real globals

rows.fidelity_note: A shared-coordinate row must have an allowed symmetry reading, valid real and imaginary components and the exact resulting row coefficients; private interior coordinates are excluded.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.KeyRow

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileSeg
ties.plain: Subsegment used by a split row

rows.fidelity_note: One subdivision segment uses its own endpoints and test coefficients at the fixed level of the original face.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileSeg
rows.plain: Subsegment used by a split row

rows.fidelity_note: The constant normal-velocity moment is recovered from endpoint stream values. The radial formula divides by the face radius, and the horizontal formula uses the nonzero leading coefficient of the linear test.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileFlux

rows.fidelity_note: The raw flux formula has assigned values even at zero denominators. Whenever the flux substitution is used, the subdivision conditions require its face radius or leading test coefficient to be nonzero.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileFlux

rows.fidelity_note: The endpoint-flux formula is used only for the constant moment of a tile designated for that substitution; other tile moments use their direct real and imaginary coordinates.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileVec

rows.fidelity_note: The intervals form a nonempty consecutive subdivision with exact polynomial test expansions, valid shared coordinates and justified flux substitutions. Their weighted sum must equal the original row exactly.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.SplitRow

rows.fidelity_note: The subdivision has positive widths, matching adjacent endpoints and the exact outer endpoints. Each test-polynomial identity holds for every real argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.SplitRow

rows.fidelity_note: Radial and horizontal faces use their respective stream-flux identities. The horizontal case also uses a valid linear velocity moment of strictly smaller dependency rank.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.FluxRow

rows.fidelity_note: The radial flux case requires positive face radius; the horizontal case requires a nonzero leading test coefficient and an available linear moment of smaller rank.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.FluxRow

rows.fidelity_note: The coefficient is the finite weighted sum of the chosen cell-relation coefficients at the selected coordinate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.relCoef

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.DerivedRow
ties.plain: Solve a relation for one row

rows.fidelity_note: The relation combination has coefficient 1 at the target and coefficient 0 at every pressure coordinate. Every other nonzero term uses an available row of smaller rank, giving a terminating reconstruction.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.DerivedRow
rows.plain: Solve a relation for one row

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.DerivedRow
ties.plain: Solve a relation for one row

rows.fidelity_note: The target coefficient is exactly 1, all pressure coefficients cancel, and each remaining dependency has strictly smaller rank. These requirements exclude cyclic reconstruction.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.DerivedRow
rows.plain: Solve a relation for one row

rows.fidelity_note: A directly read cell coordinate must supply its real component and may supply its imaginary component. Omitting the imaginary part is allowed only for the zero harmonic.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.LeafRow

rows.fidelity_note: An unused coordinate has a zero reconstruction row, zero row and column in the cell matrix and no use in a rectangle credit.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.UnusedRow

rows.fidelity_note: An unused coordinate may take any complex value in the permitted row domain. Its reconstruction row, cell-matrix row and column, and credit contributions must all vanish.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.UnusedRow

rows.fidelity_note: A velocity-trace row is returned for degrees in the specified range; beyond that range its value is zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.velRow

rows.fidelity_note: An out-of-range velocity moment returns zero. A row needed for reconstruction must separately have a valid degree, smaller rank and an active justification.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.velRow

rows.fidelity_note: A usable velocity trace has an allowed degree, a dependency rank below the target and a justification that uses the coordinate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.velReady

rows.fidelity_note: A present corner supplies its velocity row; an absent corner contributes the zero row.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cornerRow

rows.fidelity_note: All three velocity components at the corner must be available at strictly smaller dependency rank.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cornerReady

rows.fidelity_note: The normal-derivative row follows from divergence freedom, differentiated polynomial tests and endpoint velocities. The lower endpoint may be omitted only where a horizontal face starts at the axis.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.NormalRow

rows.fidelity_note: The normal-derivative identity uses a polynomial equality for every real argument, with the stated radial factors and endpoint signs. Every velocity and corner row used is available at smaller rank.
